items.summary: ⚠️ Breaking change The frontend no longer reads TRUST_X_FORWARDED_FOR ( #16530 , @Pwuts ). A self-hosted frontend that set it by hand gets no client IP from X-Forwarded-For for the sign-in IP log, IP blocks and per-visitor store search until TRUSTED_PROXIES lists the proxy in front of it. The single-container image and Vercel need nothing. What to do: if your frontend sets TRUST_X_FORWARDED_FOR , remove it and set TRUSTED_PROXIES to a comma-separated list of the addresses or CIDR ranges of the proxies in front of it. Until you do, the frontend logs a warning at start that the old setting is ignored. The same TRUSTED_PROXIES setting now also names the proxies for the backend and the External API's per-address limits, replacing FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS and TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT , which keep working but are deprecated; behind your own reverse proxy, the single-container image takes it too. See Client IP Addresses . ✨ Highlights AutoGPT in your pocket. Our new native mobile app puts your team on your phone: sign in, chat with Otto and your experts, hire experts from the Marketplace, connect your services right from the chat, and talk instead of typing with live voice dictation. ( #16715 , #16869 , #16923 , #17058 ) Get started faster. Signing up takes fewer steps (no more typing your password twice), the sign-up and login pages show up right away, and setup no longer gets stuck on "Loading your setup…". Sign up with Google and you can connect Gmail, Drive and Calendar in the same step. ( #16829 , #16831 , #16968 , #16845 , #16877 ) Safer sign-ins. Adding a new way to sign in to your account (Google, Microsoft, GitHub or Discord) now takes a six-digit code from your inbox, unless that provider runs your mailbox (Gmail through Google, Outlook.com through Microsoft). You also get an email whenever a new sign-in method is added. ( #16860 ) Never lose a message. If Otto can't confirm your message arrived, one click on Send again delivers it, files included, without sending it twice. And "Thinking…" now stays up until Otto starts answering, so you always know it's working. ( #17041 , #16962 , #17038 ) Always see where your runs really are. After a brief connection drop, your Library, run history, Activity and chats catch up on their own, so a run that already finished no longer looks like it's still going. Live updates also keep flowing on slow connections. ( #16898 , #16915 , #16932 , #16903 , #16865 , #16960 ) Schedules you can count on. During brief maintenance your schedules show as temporarily unavailable instead of disappearing, a run that comes due during a restart still runs (exactly once), and retrying a schedule you just created no longer makes a duplicate. ( #16937 , #16866 , #16919 , #16904 ) More models to choose from. Gemini 4 Neon, GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6.2 Sol and Qwen 4 Max are now available in your workflows, and Otto's advanced Codex tier now runs on GPT-6.2 Astra. ( #17023 , #16870 , #16899 , #16836 , #16852 , #16902 ) More tools for Otto. Otto can now connect to AnySearch, Supabase, Klaviyo, AI/ML API and CompanyEnrich, reads from Supabase no longer need your approval each time, and Otto now finds the custom MCP servers you've connected by URL. ( #16913 , #16659 , #16850 , #15202 , #16771 , #16447 , #15168 ) 🔒 Security This release fixes several privately reported security issues. items.summary_html:
⚠️ Breaking change

The frontend no longer reads TRUST_X_FORWARDED_FOR (#16530, @Pwuts). A self-hosted frontend that set it by hand gets no client IP from X-Forwarded-For for the sign-in IP log, IP blocks and per-visitor store search until TRUSTED_PROXIES lists the proxy in front of it. The single-container image and Vercel need nothing.

What to do: if your frontend sets TRUST_X_FORWARDED_FOR, remove it and set TRUSTED_PROXIES to a comma-separated list of the addresses or CIDR ranges of the proxies in front of it. Until you do, the frontend logs a warning at start that the old setting is ignored. The same TRUSTED_PROXIES setting now also names the proxies for the backend and the External API's per-address limits, replacing FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS and TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT, which keep working but are deprecated; behind your own reverse proxy, the single-container image takes it too. See Client IP Addresses.

✨ Highlights
  • AutoGPT in your pocket. Our new native mobile app puts your team on your phone: sign in, chat with Otto and your experts, hire experts from the Marketplace, connect your services right from the chat, and talk instead of typing with live voice dictation. (#16715, #16869, #16923, #17058)
  • Get started faster. Signing up takes fewer steps (no more typing your password twice), the sign-up and login pages show up right away, and setup no longer gets stuck on "Loading your setup…". Sign up with Google and you can connect Gmail, Drive and Calendar in the same step. (#16829, #16831, #16968, #16845, #16877)
  • Safer sign-ins. Adding a new way to sign in to your account (Google, Microsoft, GitHub or Discord) now takes a six-digit code from your inbox, unless that provider runs your mailbox (Gmail through Google, Outlook.com through Microsoft). You also get an email whenever a new sign-in method is added. (#16860)
  • Never lose a message. If Otto can't confirm your message arrived, one click on Send again delivers it, files included, without sending it twice. And "Thinking…" now stays up until Otto starts answering, so you always know it's working. (#17041, #16962, #17038)
  • Always see where your runs really are. After a brief connection drop, your Library, run history, Activity and chats catch up on their own, so a run that already finished no longer looks like it's still going. Live updates also keep flowing on slow connections. (#16898, #16915, #16932, #16903, #16865, #16960)
  • Schedules you can count on. During brief maintenance your schedules show as temporarily unavailable instead of disappearing, a run that comes due during a restart still runs (exactly once), and retrying a schedule you just created no longer makes a duplicate. (#16937, #16866, #16919, #16904)
  • More models to choose from. Gemini 4 Neon, GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6.2 Sol and Qwen 4 Max are now available in your workflows, and Otto's advanced Codex tier now runs on GPT-6.2 Astra. (#17023, #16870, #16899, #16836, #16852, #16902)
  • More tools for Otto. Otto can now connect to AnySearch, Supabase, Klaviyo, AI/ML API and CompanyEnrich, reads from Supabase no longer need your approval each time, and Otto now finds the custom MCP servers you've connected by URL. (#16913, #16659, #16850, #15202, #16771, #16447, #15168)
🔒 Security

This release fixes several privately reported security issues. We'll publish the advisories once the fixes are live in production.

🧩 Also in this release Otto and AutoPilot
  • Experts hired from chat or the API introduce themselves (#16687, @Bentlybro)
  • Measure first answer timing separately from model activity (#15533, @ntindle)
  • Measure send-to-answer timing in chat (#15541, @ntindle)
  • Let the greeting's Sonnet call think, so OpenRouter stops refusing it (#16781, @Pwuts)
  • Reword the Founder plan's third task reason (#16851, @kcze)
  • Tell Otto a refused tool call did not happen (#17036, @kcze)
  • Judge a failed tool's error text like its output (#16884, @ntindle)
  • bash_exec says when a command killed its own shell (#16347, @Pwuts)
  • List nested block output objects by field name in describe_capability (#16679, @Bentlybro)
  • Keep saved file names in the bot's reply text (#16680, @Bentlybro)
  • Don't create a second schedule for work already scheduled (#16678, @Bentlybro)
  • Consume an approval at most once (#16863, @ntindle)
  • Refund a block run whose saved review can't be read (#16895, @ntindle)
  • Back off sub-agent catch-ups while stale, and close two pub/sub gaps (#16888, @ntindle)
  • Scope find_session and message_session to the calling chat's organization (#16966, @ntindle)
  • find_session and message_session read sessions over RPC (#16858, @ntindle)
  • Keep a chat's skill index for 15 minutes so follow-ups stop rebuilding it (#15985, @ntindle)
  • Start a message's paywall and in-flight reads beside its session checks (#15779, @ntindle)
  • Read an expert's row beside its owner's scope in the turn's check (#15854, @ntindle)
  • Save a chat message without re-reading its session or its next sequence (#15486, @ntindle)
  • Save a chat message and its session's fields in one transaction (#15987, @ntindle)
Builder and workflows
  • Ctrl/Cmd+Z in a builder text field undoes the text, not the workflow (#17035, @kcze)
  • Save the builder graph from one loaded snapshot after a save (#17021, @ntindle)
  • A stored review decision wins over safe mode (#16874, @ntindle)
  • Look up a node's waiting run with a correlated query, so a busy pin name can't time it out (#16835, @Pwuts)
  • Scope four workflow and run routes to the request's organization (#16931, @Pwuts)
  • Expand Unix cron day-of-week tokens to day sets before APS mapping (#15321, @ntindle)
  • Bound custom cron intervals so APScheduler accepts them (#15322, @ntindle)
Integrations and blocks
  • Group Parallel Search MCP with native Parallel provider (#16572, @Iitian001)
  • Surface regex errors in Extract Text Information; forward falsy data in Match Text Pattern (#15313, @ntindle)
  • Read Spreadsheet handles short, ragged, duplicate-header and blank-line CSVs (#15317, @ntindle)
  • Short block input error messages (#17000, @kcze)
Platform and self-hosting
  • Boxes behind the swap proxy trust its signing CA (#16627, @kcze)
  • Refuse uploads clamd can't scan whole instead of scanning them in pieces; the bundled ClamAV's limits rise to 256M (#16694, @ntindle)
  • Resume a streamed download where storage ended early, and stop gzip holding it back (#16838, @Pwuts)
  • Harden credential masking in validation logs and error reports (#16956, @ntindle)
  • Keep request credentials out of error reports and logs (#16908, @ntindle)
  • Admin requeue publishes stuck QUEUED executions (#15328, @ntindle)
  • Report memory graph truncation only when something was cut (#16762, @67-luck)
Other fixes
  • Show a failed trial's Pay now button by reading its subscription with the card expanded (#16834, @Pwuts)
  • Prevent translation extensions from breaking suggested tasks on Home (#16776, @sentry[bot])
  • Stop the avatar image hang and drop networkidle waits from e2e (#17013, @ntindle)

Dependencies: 5 bumps (#16945, #16943, #16944, #16946, #16947).

CI, tests and developer tooling: 11 changes (#17012, #16799, #16832, #16918, #16842, #16924, #16914, #16930, #16876, #16859, #16928).

Documentation: 3 changes (#17002, #16892, #16519).

🎉 Thanks to our contributors

@ntindle, @Bentlybro, @67-luck, @Pwuts, @kcze, @Lookoff-AIMLAPI, @Iitian001, @namirali, @ayush-singh-0601, @0ubbe

Full Changelog: autogpt-platform-beta-v0.11.3...autogpt-platform-beta-v0.12.0

📝 Feedback and issues

If you encounter any issues or have suggestions, please join our Discord and let us know!

items.summary_html:
What's Changed Features
  • Add capability to save files as versioned, shareable artifacts.
Bug Fixes
  • Fix inline agent and crew action references relative to the flow file.
  • Stop duplicating kept separators when merging chunks.
  • Isolate nested defaults from a shared flow declaration.
  • Restrict Pillow to PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WEBP when opening images.
  • Reset cache eviction order on clear.
  • Treat a docs path on GitHub as a repository.
  • Exit with the script's status when crewai train fails.
  • Relax av pin to ensure current FFmpeg installs.
  • Keep a deeply nested span that the run app cannot render as text in one step.
  • Stop stamping cache_control on every anthropic file block.
  • Detect vision for any Claude 3+ model and geo profile.
  • Export structured output from non-str guardrail results.
  • Enforce cwd containment for all FilePath paths.
Documentation
  • Teach the flow skill to save and read artifacts.
Contributors

HanYuanLu, Kiko0301, Vidit Ostwal (@Vidit-Ostwal), T Mohan Aditya (@adityajai119), anilkr09, Gabe Milani (@gabemilani), João Moura (@joaomdmoura), Marcus Kuquert (@kuquert), Nurlan Mammadli (@nurlanmnn), willnhansen

items.title: Show HN: AgentMall – Let your AI agent buy groceries
items.summary: Hey HN, we’re Nel and Kosi. We noticed personal agents like Instinct, Muse were terrible at buying stuff. Most of the time the checkout would fail. So we built reliable automations for agents to checkout at 9 leading grocery merchants. We grapple with anti bot, logins, OTP codes, and changing checkout structures. Loved revisiting this stuff given our backgrounds sneaker-botting and building computer use models. Honestly full circle haha. It currently works on these sites with ~70% checkout success rate: - Walmart - Albertsons - Ocado - Wegmans - FreshDirect - Best Buy - Instacart Our goal is to hill climb to 90%+ across each. Test keys are free and run the real flow without placing an order. New accounts get 10 free completed orders. https://docs.getagentmall.com/quickstart

items.title: Releasing Typemaid on NPM Turning your mermaid diagrams into AI workflows
items.summary: I've been privately building a TypeScript SDK called TypeMaid and using it for my own projects over the past month. It's based on Typed DAGs, with Mermaid diagrams to define and visualize AI workflows. I've found this approach surprisingly simple to understand and work with, especially compared to writing workflows entirely in code. I recently open-sourced it and am now working on durability, retries, and persistent execution. I'm curious what others think about using Mermaid to define executable AI workflows. Does this approach make sense, or am I missing something? Would really appreciate any feedback, suggestions, or contributions! Star on github https://github.com/typemaid/typemaid

items.title: Preview seed fixture (rolling)
items.summary: Rolling, fully SYNTHETIC preview-database seed fixture baked from dev@6a42315fec58 (migration head: 20261112120000_account_deletion_confirmation_skipped). Preview environments restore fixture.dump.gz (custom-format, gzipped, platform schema only, including _prisma_migrations) BEFORE running a PR's own migrations, so schema changes run against populated tables. RESTORE: apply restore-preamble.sql to the target database first (it creates the platform schema and installs the vector + pg_trgm extensions into it, which pg_dump --schema=platform omits), then run 'gunzip -c fixture.dump.gz | pg_restore -d --no-owner' WITHOUT --exit-on-error (the dump's own CREATE SCHEMA collides benignly with the preamble's). SECURITY INVARIANT: this bake holds no cloud credentials and has no read path to any real database — it runs entirely against a throwaway Postgres container and contains only synthetic rows (Faker-generated, plus the hand-written preview marketplace) and the already-public marketplace agent exports checked into autogpt_platform/backend/agents/. This asset is regenerated on every eligible dev push and weekly; treat it as disposable.

items.title: Vercel Billing CLI is now available
items.summary: You can now check your team’s billing overview, review and download invoices, and preview upcoming charges with the Vercel CLI . All billing commands, including usage, contracts, and budgets, are now grouped under vercel billing . Billing overview and invoice history are available on all plans, subject to your team’s existing billing permissions. Upcoming invoice estimates require an active paid subscription. Billing overview Check your team’s plan, billing status, billing cycle, balance due, and overdue invoices: In CLI 65.17.0 and later, this overview also includes configured invoice details such as your billing address, tax ID, and purchase order. Invoices and upcoming charges Use vercel billing invoices to review invoices, download PDFs, and preview upcoming charges. For inspect and download , replace with a full invoice ID from the list output: Upcoming charges are estimates and may change until the end of the billing period. For scripts and agents, add --json to vercel billing overview or any vercel billing invoices subcommand for structured output. Existing usage, contract, and budget commands now also use the same prefix: vercel usage → vercel billing usage vercel contract → vercel billing contract vercel budgets → vercel billing budgets The previous command names continue to work as aliases. To get started, update your Vercel CLI with vercel upgrade . Learn more in the Billing & Invoices documentation .
items.summary_html:
You can now check your team’s billing overview, review and download invoices, and preview upcoming charges with the Vercel CLI. All billing commands, including usage, contracts, and budgets, are now grouped under vercel billing.

Billing overview and invoice history are available on all plans, subject to your team’s existing billing permissions. Upcoming invoice estimates require an active paid subscription.

Billing overview

Check your team’s plan, billing status, billing cycle, balance due, and overdue invoices:

In CLI 65.17.0 and later, this overview also includes configured invoice details such as your billing address, tax ID, and purchase order.

Invoices and upcoming charges

Use vercel billing invoices to review invoices, download PDFs, and preview upcoming charges. For inspect and download, replace with a full invoice ID from the list output:

Upcoming charges are estimates and may change until the end of the billing period.

For scripts and agents, add --json to vercel billing overview or any vercel billing invoices subcommand for structured output.

Existing usage, contract, and budget commands now also use the same prefix:

  • vercel usage → vercel billing usage

  • vercel contract → vercel billing contract

  • vercel budgets → vercel billing budgets

The previous command names continue to work as aliases.

items.summary_html:
Coding agents can now use vercel help search to find Vercel CLI commands by describing a task in plain language.

The search returns a list of matching commands. Add --with-help to include the help page for the first result in the same call. For example, vercel help search "roll back production" --with-help returns the options and examples for vercel rollback.

Search also supports:

  • API endpoints: When a Vercel API endpoint matches the task, search returns a vercel api command with the request path and placeholders for every required input. The agent can fill in the values without guessing the path.

  • JSON output: Use --json to return search results as JSON. Combine it with --with-help to include usage instructions, options, and examples for the first result.

Search recognizes common wording, such as “show” instead of “list,” and handles minor spelling mistakes.

The CLI also includes a skill that tells coding agents to start with vercel help search when looking for a command. Vercel doesn't log your search text.

Update to the latest Vercel CLI with vercel upgrade.

items.title: Madras School System and AI Learning Share Similarity
items.summary: Madras School education system (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madras_School) that was the bedrock of mass public structured education in the late 18-19th century has several similarities on how AI is trained today. They both ensures that knowledge dissemination is free. The similarities they share are as follows 1) Madras school & AI distillation (Teacher-Student models) encourages Students to teach others instead of just teachers thereby reducing cost. 2) Madras school & Reinforcement learning rewards or awards penalty scores based on the assessment/feedback. 3) Both systems ultimately ended in rote learning and hallucinations. The other day when I noticed that several leading professors of top universities were sharing their top courses for free on YT. I immediately remembered our education system (Madras School) and how it had a profound impact in today's education system especially public mass elementary schooling system. It is also notable that today's AI training took a leaf out of it. Those professors were indeed trying to bring Madras school system to the Universities by free knowledge dissemination that too in this AI era, which is commendable. But the current commercial education system is a stark difference from the Madras school which was designed for the mass and was affordable. But today's education and research is full of competition and highly unaffordable which was not the case in the early 19th century. Finally, I would like to conclude that the commercial education (training teachers) and proprietary SOTA frontier models both gate keep their highest tier capabilities behind high tuition or API paywalls, whereas open weights models and the Madras System prioritize broad, low cost knowledge dissemination.

items.title: Ask HN: What positive impact has AI had in the past 5 years?
items.summary: I asked myself this question this morning and I swear I couldn't find one single thing. We still have all the problems we had before AI. AI did not solve the climate collapse, did not cure cancer, did not figure society-altering new technologies, did not make politics not suck anymore, did not solve our anxieties... If anything, we're all just more anxious today. It succeeded at making my work toxic because of the cyber warfare paranoia, I guess. AI successfully blew and continues to blow all the benchmarks it's been trained to blow. It makes long mathematical proofs nobody can read or verify about problems nobody cares about. Great? So… can someone list things that AI has genuinely improved? If there are none, why do we tolerate it?

items.title: Show HN: Disposable – Share small AI-made tools so others can rebuild them
items.summary: I made a site for sharing small tools made with AI. With agents, it is now quick to build a tool that fits your own task. But those tools usually get thrown away after use, and the next person who may needs something similar start again from zero. So I thought maybe if result or process could shared by text or code and this can lead to kind of token sharing economy. Its name is Disposable and compared to "Open source", I named its philosophy to "Open Disposable". So the principle is "Like open source, without the upkeep. Keep the know-how, rebuild the tool your way". You can share anything you actually used and found useful, with no promise to maintain it. Others can use it as is, or give the spec that comes with it to theur own agent and have it rebuilt. If you have your own skill, prompt, or program you would like to show others, please share it. If you get stuck while sharing, let me know. Repo: https://github.com/x-ify/disposable

items.summary: Priority Projects are now in public beta for Pro and Enterprise teams. This optional upgrade for individual Vercel projects adds bot and traffic-source signals, Page Integrity for monitoring and controlling client-side scripts and connections, and additional Firewall controls and alerts. Bot signals Bot protection is free on all plans. You can enable it to challenge non-browser traffic while allowing verified bots. Priority adds more detailed bot signals: categories, verification status, and names where available. Use these signals in: Firewall rules: Match on bot_name , bot_category , bot_status , and bot_protection in the dashboard or with vercel firewall rules add . Application code: Read x-vercel-bot-category , x-vercel-bot-name , and x-vercel-verified-bot from request headers in Routing Middleware and Vercel Functions. See the header reference for verified and claimed bot names. Logs and Observability: Logs show the Firewall action on all plans. Priority adds the matched rule and bot details where available. In Firewall Observability, Priority adds botCategory for unverified traffic. Log Drains also include bot classifications. Traffic Sources Priority adds Traffic Sources labels for requests from Tor exit nodes, VPNs, open or anonymizing proxies, and residential proxies. It also labels traffic flagged by abuse blocklists. Use these labels in custom Firewall rules, analyze them in Firewall Observability, or read them from the x-vercel-waf-source request header in your application. A request can have multiple labels. Use the Traffic Sources managed ruleset to log, challenge, or block traffic by source category. Review matching traffic before enabling blocking, since these categories can also include legitimate users. To enable the Traffic Sources managed ruleset from the CLI, run vercel firewall managed-rulesets enable traffic-sources . This stages the change; review it with vercel firewall diff , then apply it with vercel firewall publish . Page Integrity Priority Projects get access to Page Integrity to monitor client-side scripts and connections, receive alerts when new scripts or connections are detected, and block unapproved resources. Page Integrity maintains a resource inventory and uses Content Security Policy (CSP) for discovery and enforcement, without adding client-side JavaScript. It operates in three stages: Detect: Discover scripts using report-only CSP headers on sampled requests. Review: Approve or reject scripts and record business justifications. Block: Enforce a CSP that blocks scripts outside the approved inventory. Page Integrity must be enabled separately. Configure monitoring and review resources in the dashboard; the CLI can also show its resource inventory: Firewall controls and alerts Anomaly alerts DDoS alerts are available on all plans. Priority adds anomaly alerts for bot traffic and requests matching system or custom Firewall rules. Use these alerts to investigate potential attacks and unusual traffic patterns. Configure notifications in your team’s Settings > Alerts , with delivery options including email, Slack, and webhooks. View recent alerts with vercel alerts --since 24h . To manage alert configuration from the CLI, see vercel monitors . OWASP Core Ruleset On Pro, Priority lets you enable the OWASP Core Ruleset to protect against common web application attacks. Enterprise projects can already enable it without Priority. Add it as a team default from Security > Rules , or enable it for a linked project via the CLI with vercel firewall managed-rulesets enable owasp --yes followed by vercel firewall publish . OWASP inspection is billed separately per inspected request and GB of inspected payload. Response-based rate limiting Priority adds response conditions to the rate-limit rules available on all plans. Count requests toward a limit only when their responses match specified HTTP status codes or response headers. For example, count 401 responses from failed login attempts or 404 responses for missing pages, rather than every matching request. items.summary_html:
Priority Projects are now in public beta for Pro and Enterprise teams. This optional upgrade for individual Vercel projects adds bot and traffic-source signals, Page Integrity for monitoring and controlling client-side scripts and connections, and additional Firewall controls and alerts.

Bot signals

Bot protection is free on all plans. You can enable it to challenge non-browser traffic while allowing verified bots. Priority adds more detailed bot signals: categories, verification status, and names where available. Use these signals in:

  • Firewall rules: Match on bot_name, bot_category, bot_status, and bot_protection in the dashboard or with vercel firewall rules add.

  • Application code: Read x-vercel-bot-category, x-vercel-bot-name, and x-vercel-verified-bot from request headers in Routing Middleware and Vercel Functions. See the header reference for verified and claimed bot names.

  • Logs and Observability: Logs show the Firewall action on all plans. Priority adds the matched rule and bot details where available. In Firewall Observability, Priority adds botCategory for unverified traffic. Log Drains also include bot classifications.

Traffic Sources

Priority adds Traffic Sources labels for requests from Tor exit nodes, VPNs, open or anonymizing proxies, and residential proxies. It also labels traffic flagged by abuse blocklists.

Use these labels in custom Firewall rules, analyze them in Firewall Observability, or read them from the x-vercel-waf-source request header in your application. A request can have multiple labels.

Use the Traffic Sources managed ruleset to log, challenge, or block traffic by source category. Review matching traffic before enabling blocking, since these categories can also include legitimate users.

To enable the Traffic Sources managed ruleset from the CLI, run vercel firewall managed-rulesets enable traffic-sources. This stages the change; review it with vercel firewall diff, then apply it with vercel firewall publish.

Page Integrity

Priority Projects get access to Page Integrity to monitor client-side scripts and connections, receive alerts when new scripts or connections are detected, and block unapproved resources.

Page Integrity maintains a resource inventory and uses Content Security Policy (CSP) for discovery and enforcement, without adding client-side JavaScript.

It operates in three stages:

  • Detect: Discover scripts using report-only CSP headers on sampled requests.

  • Review: Approve or reject scripts and record business justifications.

  • Block: Enforce a CSP that blocks scripts outside the approved inventory.

Page Integrity must be enabled separately. Configure monitoring and review resources in the dashboard; the CLI can also show its resource inventory:

Firewall controls and alertsAnomaly alerts

DDoS alerts are available on all plans. Priority adds anomaly alerts for bot traffic and requests matching system or custom Firewall rules. Use these alerts to investigate potential attacks and unusual traffic patterns.

Configure notifications in your team’s Settings > Alerts, with delivery options including email, Slack, and webhooks.

View recent alerts with vercel alerts --since 24h. To manage alert configuration from the CLI, see vercel monitors.

OWASP Core Ruleset

On Pro, Priority lets you enable the OWASP Core Ruleset to protect against common web application attacks. Enterprise projects can already enable it without Priority.

Add it as a team default from Security > Rules, or enable it for a linked project via the CLI with vercel firewall managed-rulesets enable owasp --yes followed by vercel firewall publish. OWASP inspection is billed separately per inspected request and GB of inspected payload.

Response-based rate limiting

Priority adds response conditions to the rate-limit rules available on all plans. Count requests toward a limit only when their responses match specified HTTP status codes or response headers. For example, count 401 responses from failed login attempts or 404 responses for missing pages, rather than every matching request.

Higher Firewall limits

Priority increases the following per-project limits (shown as standard → with Priority):

Get started

Priority costs $200 per project per month. Enable it from your project’s Firewall or Settings page, or with the CLI.

For the CLI, update to the latest version with vercel upgrade, then enable Priority for the project you want to upgrade:

Page Integrity usage is billed separately. Its standard rate is $2 per 1,000 monitored page views, with each view covering up to 100 scripts.

Learn more in the Priority Projects documentation.

items.title: GPT-Live 1.1 now available on AI Gateway
items.summary: GPT-Live 1.1 from OpenAI is now available on AI Gateway. GPT-Live 1.1 is a full-duplex voice model, so it listens while it speaks and a caller can pause, interrupt, or add detail mid-reply. Compared with the previous GPT-Live model, it transcribes speech more accurately and keeps a more consistent accent and voice across languages. It uses the same Live endpoint and client delegation, so an existing GPT-Live integration only needs the new model ID. Simple example without delegation Run openai/gpt-live-1.1 by itself: Delegate work and keep talking Turn on client delegation, and use the session instructions to tell GPT-Live 1.1 when to ask for help. It asks by sending delegation-created. Answer with any text model on AI Gateway and return the result on the commentary channel for GPT-Live to speak. This example uses openai/gpt-6.2-sol and builds on the session above: Your application controls delegated work and its permissions, confirmations, and cancellation. Delegated model requests are billed separately through AI Gateway, and voice-session usage continues while they run. These snippets omit the WebSocket connection, event parsing, transcript assembly, audio streaming, and shutdown. See the GPT-Live guide for connection setup, audio streaming, and complete examples. Try GPT-Live 1.1 in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all models available on AI Gateway.

items.title: Liquid AI's d1.2 and d1.2-ultra are now available on AI Gateway
items.summary: Liquid AI’s d1.2 and d1.2-ultra are now available on AI Gateway with audio input and bounding box support. These decision models return structured answers instead of generating text. Ask Boolean questions for yes/no probabilities, Choice questions to select a category, or Score questions to rate an input against a rubric. Multiple questions can share the same input in one request. d1.2 is the faster, lower-cost model. d1.2-ultra is Liquid AI’s most accurate decision model. Use liquid/d1.2 or liquid/d1.2-ultra as the model name. Before running the examples, set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY to an AI Gateway API key . Classify a voicemail with AI SDK 7 Pass audio as a file part in state . This example reads voicemail.flac and returns the probability that the caller is requesting a refund. It requires ai 7.0.136 or later. For image classification, pass image bytes with the matching media type, such as image/png . Locate an object with the Decisions API Box questions return top and bottom as fractions of the image height, and left and right as fractions of its width. This Python example uses the Decisions API to locate a signature in form.png and print its bounding box: Decision requests appear in AI Gateway logs and count toward budgets . Learn more in the decision model documentation , or browse all decision models .
